'''Christa Schleper''' is a German [[microbiologist]] known for her work on the evolution and ecology of [[Archaea]]. Schleper is Head of the Department of Functional and Evolutionary Biology at the [[University of Vienna]] in Austria.

== Life and education ==
Having initially gone to university to study languages and economics, Schleper eventually switched to studying biology.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pioneer in archaea research (Christa Schleper) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2F6XsDD4OPI |website=YouTube | date=21 August 2023 |access-date=3 November 2023 |language=en}}</ref> She received a Ph.D. at the [[Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry]] in 1995 and subsequently did postdoctoral research at the [[Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Albers |first=Sonja-Verena |title=Christa Schleper: Enthusiasm and Insight in the World of Archaea |publisher=American Society for Microbiology |year=2018 |location=Washington, DC |pages=253–256 |author-link=Sonja-Verena Albers}}</ref>

== Work and discoveries ==

Schleper is known for research advancing understanding of uncultivated Archaea in marine and terrestrial systems. Schleper's early research on ''Sulfolobus'' was the first research to indicate the presence of a virus in a thermophilic Archaea.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Schleper|first1=C.|last2=Kubo|first2=K.|last3=Zillig|first3=W.|date=15 August 1992|title=The particle SSV1 from the extremely thermophilic archaeon Sulfolobus is a virus: demonstration of infectivity and of transfection with viral DNA.|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=89|issue=16|pages=7645–7649|doi=10.1073/pnas.89.16.7645|issn=0027-8424|pmc=49767|pmid=1502176|bibcode=1992PNAS...89.7645S|doi-access=free}}</ref> Schleper went on to isolate multiple thermophilic Archaea capable of growth under acidic conditions,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Schleper|first=Christa|date=1995|title=Picrophilus gen. nov., fam. nov.: a novel aerobic, heterotrophic, thermoacidophilic genus and family comprising archaea capable of growth around pH 0.|journal=Journal of Bacteriology|volume=177|issue=24|pages=7050–7059|doi=10.1128/jb.177.24.7050-7059.1995|pmid=8522509|pmc=177581}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Schleper|first1=Christa|last2=Piihler|first2=Gabriela|last3=Kuhlmorgen|first3=Brigitte|last4=Zillig|first4=Wolfram|date=June 1995|title=Life at extremely low pH|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/375741b0|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=375|issue=6534|pages=741–742|doi=10.1038/375741b0|pmid=7541113|bibcode=1995Natur.375..741S|s2cid=4341809|issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and led 16S RNA surveys to define the distribution of crenarchaeota in terrestrial environments.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Quaiser|first1=Achim|last2=Ochsenreiter|first2=Torsten|last3=Lanz|first3=Christa|last4=Schuster|first4=Stephan C.|last5=Treusch|first5=Alexander H.|last6=Eck|first6=Jürgen|last7=Schleper|first7=Christa|date=2003|title=Acidobacteria form a coherent but highly diverse group within the bacterial domain: evidence from environmental genomics|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1046/j.1365-2958.2003.03707.x|journal=Molecular Microbiology|language=en|volume=50|issue=2|pages=563–575|doi=10.1046/j.1365-2958.2003.03707.x|pmid=14617179|s2cid=25162803|issn=1365-2958|url-access=subscription}}</ref> During postdoctoral research, Schleper used biochemical information from a low-temperature crenarchaeota to propose a non-thermophilic origin for these crenarchaeota, a novel idea at the time it was proposed in 1997.<ref>{{Cite |inventor4=Frank Niehaus;Sonja-Verena Albers;Sabrina Froels}}</ref> and Nucleic acids and proteins from ''Cenarchaeum symbiosum''.<ref>{{cite patent |country=WO|number=0018909|pubdate=2000-07-27|title=Nucleic acids and proteins from ''Cenarchaeum symbiosum''|assign1=[[Diversa|Diversa Corp.]]|inventor1-last=Swanson|inventor1-first=Ronald V.|inventor2-last=Feldman|inventor2-first=Robert A.|inventor3-last=Schleper|inventor3-first=Christa}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==

* 2001 [[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]] Young Investigator Award<ref>{{Cite web|title=Find an EMBO Young Investigator / EMBO Installation Grantee / EMBO Global Investigator|url=https://yip-search.embo.org/#/yip/2237|access-date=5 May 2021|website=yip-search.embo.org}}</ref>
* 2011 Elected member of the American Academy of Microbiology<ref>{{Cite web|title=American Academy of Microbiology Fellows|url=https://asm.org/Academy/Academy|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190104191743/https://www.asm.org/Academy/Academy |archive-date=4 January 2019 }}</ref>
* 2017 Elected full member of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=ÖAW Mitglieder Detail|url=https://www.oeaw.ac.at/en/m/schleper-christa|access-date=5 May 2021|website=www.oeaw.ac.at}}</ref>
* 2022 [[Wittgenstein Award]]<ref name="DER STANDARD 2022">{{cite web | title=Mikrobiologin Christa Schleper erhält den diesjährigen "Austro-Nobelpreis" | website=[[Der Standard]] | date=22 June 2022 | url=https://www.derstandard.at/story/2000136798596/mikrobiologin-christa-schleper-erhaelt-den-diesjaehrigen-austro-nobelpreis | language=de | access-date=23 June 2022}}</ref>
